_meta.challenge: Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data
_meta.purpose: Knowledge base of NASA microgravity combustion findings. Feeds (1) simulation parameters, (2) AI analyst context, (3) Findings Explorer (summarize / rank / interpret).
_meta.status: v0.2 - aligned with the challenge statement (PSI investigations list, habitats, attributes)

findings.platform: Cygnus cargo vehicle, after ISS departure
findings.key_finding: First large-scale fire set inside a spacecraft. Flames reached a steady size and spread rate instead of accelerating as on Earth. Flame speed scaled with the forced airflow velocity. Vehicle size affected the fire more than expected.
findings.sim_use: Flame spread rate proportional to ventilation airflow; base value 1.8 mm/s at 20 cm/s.
findings.safety_implication: Ventilation directly feeds and drives a microgravity fire; cutting airflow is a first-line action.
findings.objective: Flame spread, mass consumption and heat release of a large-scale fire inside a real spacecraft; verify low-g flammability limits
findings.fuel: Thin cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) sheet 94 x 40.6 cm; Saffire-II: 9 samples 5 x 30 cm (silicone, PMMA, SIBAL, Nomex)
findings.measurements: Video, radiometers, thermocouples, O2 and CO2 sensors
findings.short: Flames reach a steady size; spread scales with airflow

findings.key_finding: Temperature and pressure rise in the vehicle were less significant than the rise in CO and CO2. Temperature rose significantly only very near the fire. Ambient CO exceeded the 24-hour crew limit in PMMA tests. HF and HCl acid gases were measured and transported through the vehicle.
findings.sim_use: CO is the leading indicator; temperature sensors only react when near the source. Weight CO higher than temperature in the risk score for remote zones.
findings.safety_implication: Detection must rely on gas (CO) and particulates, not just temperature; post-fire cleanup matters.
findings.objective: Fire growth on thick fuels, impact on the vehicle, detection, monitoring and post-fire cleanup
findings.hardware: Saffire Flow Unit + Far Field Diagnostics in Cygnus
findings.fuel: SIBAL cloth, cotton jersey, PMMA slabs 0.5-1 cm, Nomex
findings.measurements: Temperature at 6 locations, CO2, CO, O2, HF, HCl, aerosols, combustion products monitor, smoke eater

findings.key_finding: Materials can burn at lower oxygen concentration in microgravity than in normal gravity when there is adequate ventilation. Flames extinguish at very low flow (quenching) and very high flow (blowoff).
findings.sim_use: Flammability boundary: flame sustained only if O2 above limit for the current airflow; limit is ~1 point lower in microgravity than 1g.
findings.safety_implication: Earth-based flammability screening (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) may not be conservative for microgravity.
findings.objective: Ignition, flame growth, spread and extinction limits of solids in low-speed forced flow; bridge NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 to microgravity
findings.hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), modular fan-driven flow duct
findings.fuel: PMMA rods, sheets and slabs; cotton-fiberglass fabric
findings.short: Burns at lower O₂ in microgravity (17% vs 18%)

findings.experiment: SoFIE (Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction): GEL, MIST, SMuRF
findings.key_finding: Studies ignition and extinction of real spacecraft materials in exploration atmospheres. Radiative quenching observed when flow velocity drops below about 2 cm/s. Goals include optimal suppression by diluents, flow reduction and venting.
findings.sim_use: If ventilation is cut below ~2 cm/s, flame enters quenching regime (supports 'stop ventilation' recommendation).
findings.safety_implication: Flow reduction is a valid suppression method in microgravity.
findings.objective: Ignition and flammability of solid spacecraft materials in exploration atmospheres; suppression by diluents, flow reduction, venting
findings.hardware: SoFIE insert in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
findings.fuel: PMMA sphere 4 cm (GEL), PMMA cylinders (MIST), engineering materials (SMuRF)
findings.o2: Variable incl. space exploration atmospheres (e.g. 17.5% start in GEL)

findings.key_finding: Measured how inert diluents (CO2, He) extinguish flames in microgravity. Discovered 'cool flames': after the visible flame went out, large heptane droplets kept burning invisibly.
findings.sim_use: Suppression verification must not rely on optical flame detection alone; keep monitoring temperature and CO after apparent extinction.
findings.safety_implication: A fire can look extinguished but still burn: verify with gas and temperature before declaring safe.
findings.objective: Inert-gas suppressant efficacy and limiting oxygen index for droplet flames
findings.hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in CIR
findings.measurements: Backlit droplet view, orthogonal flame view, radiometers
findings.short: Flames can keep burning invisibly (cool flames)

findings.key_finding: Smoke from overheated spacecraft materials is mostly below 500 nm. The ISS light-scattering detector often missed the small particles from Teflon and Kapton, which are used extensively in electronics, the most likely fire source in space.
findings.sim_use: Particle sensor for electronics zones should track small (sub-micron) particles; pre-fire overheating produces smoke before flame.
findings.safety_implication: Electronics bay needs detectors tuned for Teflon/Kapton smoke, plus CO.
findings.objective: Smoke particle size from overheated spacecraft materials to design better smoke detectors
findings.fuel: Teflon, Kapton, cellulose, silicone rubber, Pyrell (heated below ignition)
findings.measurements: Aerosol moment instruments, TEM grids, ISS and Shuttle smoke detectors, P-Trak (from DAFT)

findings.key_finding: ISS fire response: turn off ventilation, remove power from the affected unit, then use extinguishers (CO2 on US segment). Smoke detectors are placed in the ventilation system because smoke does not rise.
findings.sim_use: Defines the recommended action sequence shown in the AI popup: 1) stop ventilation, 2) cut power, 3) release suppressant.
findings.safety_implication: Labeeb's recommendations align with NASA's operational fire response.
findings.objective: Operational fire detection, isolation, suppression and recovery on ISS
findings.hardware: ISS smoke detectors in ventilation, portable CO2 extinguishers, breathing apparatus

findings.key_finding: NASA recommends 8.2 psia / 34% O2 for Moon/Mars missions. Material flammability is the most critical hurdle in this atmosphere.
findings.sim_use: Scenario presets: ISS air (21% / 101 kPa) and Exploration Atmosphere (34% / 56.5 kPa). Replaces the unrealistic 61% O2.
findings.safety_implication: Future vehicles will run at higher O2 fraction, raising fire risk; protection layers matter more.
findings.objective: Habitat atmosphere balancing EVA prebreathe, hypoxia and flammability

findings.experiment: FM2 (Flammability of Materials on the Moon)
findings.key_finding: First combustion experiment planned on another planetary body. Microgravity combustion is a different regime from partial gravity; some materials may hit a buoyancy 'sweet spot' in reduced gravity where burning is sustained rather than suppressed.
findings.sim_use: Gravity selector: lunar/Mars gravity adds weak buoyant flow, so a flame can persist even with ventilation off; confidence is lowered because no flight data exists yet.
findings.safety_implication: Microgravity data alone does not close the lunar/Mars gap; partial-gravity worst case must be checked.
findings.objective: Material flammability in lunar gravity: first combustion experiment on another planetary body
findings.hardware: Self-contained chamber on a CLPS lunar lander
findings.short: No flight data yet for lunar gravity

findings.key_finding: Develops a method to relate material flammability limits measured in normal gravity to microgravity.
findings.sim_use: Justifies applying a microgravity correction to Earth-measured material limits (we lower the limiting O2 by ~1 point, per BASS-II).
findings.safety_implication: Material screening for spacecraft needs reduced-gravity correction.
findings.objective: Relate normal-gravity flammability limits to microgravity
findings.short: Links 1 g flammability limits to microgravity

findings.objective: Six gaseous-flame experiments on one modular hardware set: cleaner combustion, soot, cool flames, electric fields, burning-rate emulation
findings.fuel: Gaseous fuels (e.g. propane, methane, ethylene) on burners
findings.gravity: Microgravity; E-FIELD Flames mimics partial gravity with electric fields
findings.key_finding: ACME's Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) burned gaseous fuels to study material flammability as a function of material properties. Cool Flames with Gases (CFI-G) ran the highest O2 in microgravity tests, with up to 85% O2 flowing from a spherical burner (inside-out flame). E-FIELD Flames used an electric field on flame ions to mimic partial gravity.
findings.sim_use: High-O2 behaviour (spacesuit / exploration atmospheres) and the only PSI proxy for partial gravity (E-FIELD).
findings.safety_implication: Material flammability can be estimated from material properties; partial gravity can be bounded between 0 g and 1 g.
findings.short: Gaseous flames up to 85% O₂; partial-gravity proxy

findings.experiment: CFI and FLEX-2 (Cool Flames Investigation, droplet combustion)
findings.objective: Droplet burning, cool-flame chemistry and extinction of liquid fuels
findings.hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in CIR
findings.key_finding: Follow-on droplet campaigns in the same MDCA hardware as FLEX. Large n-alkane droplets keep burning quasi-steadily in a low-temperature 'cool flame' regime after the hot flame goes out.
findings.sim_use: Reinforces post-extinction verification with CO and temperature.
findings.safety_implication: Invisible low-temperature burning can follow apparent extinction.
findings.short: Cool-flame burning after the hot flame goes out

findings.experiment: SPICE and SLICE (co-flow jet diffusion flames)
findings.objective: Smoke point, stability, lift-off and extinction of laminar jet diffusion flames
findings.hardware: MSG with the modular fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE
findings.measurements: Color imaging, flame shape and lift-off height
findings.key_finding: Characterized smoke point and flame stability without buoyancy; SLICE flames have accurate numerical models. Same MSG flow duct later used by BASS and BASS-II.
findings.sim_use: Background physics for soot / smoke generation; model validation data.
findings.safety_implication: Soot and smoke behaviour differs in microgravity, affecting detection.
findings.short: Soot and flame stability without buoyancy

findings.experiment: DAFT and DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test)
findings.objective: Test whether a modified P-Trak particle counter works in microgravity
findings.key_finding: An instrument used for smoke detection in SAME / SAME-R was first used to detect dust in DAFT and DAFT-2, showing background dust must be separated from smoke.
findings.sim_use: Particle sensor baseline: background dust offset before smoke alarm.
findings.safety_implication: False alarms from dust must be filtered in spacecraft detectors.
findings.short: Dust must be separated from smoke in detectors
